intervals.note: IceTop stations were installed on top of the IceCube strings during the 2004–2010 construction seasons, but the collaboration does not publish IceTop-specific start or completion dates; the start of full 86-string operation is used.
intervals.quote: IceTop consists of 81 stations located on top of the same number of IceCube strings. Each station has two tanks, each equipped with two downward facing DOMs.

name: IceTop
notes: The area covered by IceTop (≈1 km², matching the in-ice array footprint) is not stated on the fetched official pages and is not recorded.

placements.note: IceTop stations sit on the surface above the IceCube strings; no separate deployment start is published, so the start of full 86-string operation is used.
placements.quote: IceTop consists of 81 stations located on top of the same number of IceCube strings. Each station has two tanks, each equipped with two downward facing DOMs.

altitude.note: Ice-surface elevation of the South Pole station given by NSF; IceTop sits at that surface.
altitude.quote: Positioned at 90°S, the geographic South Pole. Sits atop the Antarctic ice sheet at an elevation of approximately 2,835 meters (9,301 feet) above sea level.

energy_range.quote: IceTop, built as a veto and calibration detector for IceCube, also detects air showers from primary cosmic rays in the 300 TeV to 1 EeV energy range.
energy_range.value: Air showers from primary cosmic rays in the 300 TeV to 1 EeV energy range

summary.plain: The part of IceCube that sits on the snow surface: 81 pairs of frozen water tanks that catch the showers of particles made when cosmic rays hit the atmosphere. It also helps IceCube tell cosmic rays apart from neutrinos.
summary.technical: Surface air-shower array of 162 ice-filled Cherenkov tanks in 81 stations (324 DOMs) above the IceCube strings; serves as a cosmic-ray veto and calibration detector and measures cosmic-ray flux, composition and Southern-Hemisphere arrival directions from 300 TeV to 1 EeV.
